purpose: Sinecatechins is used to treat external genital warts and warts around the anal area in adults who have healthy immune systems. It does not cure the virus that causes warts, but it helps make the warts go away. It is not used inside the vagina, anus, or urethra.
how_it_works: This medicine is made from a green tea plant extract and contains natural compounds called catechins. These compounds work by helping your immune system fight the wart-causing virus and may also directly interfere with the wart cells' ability to survive and grow. Think of it like green tea antioxidants working on your skin to help your body clear the warts on its own.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects happen right where you apply the ointment. You may notice redness, swelling, burning, itching, or pain at the treated area. Some people also experience skin sores, flaking, or a discharge in the treated area. These reactions are usually manageable but can sometimes be uncomfortable.
warnings: Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant, as its safety in pregnancy has not been established. Avoid getting the ointment in your eyes, mouth, nose, or inside your body openings — it is for external use only. Do not wash the treated area right after applying it. It can weaken condoms and diaphragms, so use other birth control methods while on this medicine. Tell your doctor if you are immunocompromised, as this medicine is not approved for people with weakened immune systems.
typical_dosing: You apply a small amount — about a half-inch strand — of the ointment to each wart three times a day, every day, until the warts are completely gone. Do not use it for more than 16 weeks. Wash your hands before and after applying, and try not to cover the area with a bandage unless your doctor tells you to.
